notes: "One morning, a bamboo was full of light." 'a bamboo' as a count noun is slightly odd; consider "One morning, one bamboo was full of light." or "One piece of bamboo was full of light."
"His men took the drink up Mount Fuji. There, they burned it." Burning a drink is a little strange for a learner; consider "There, they put the drink and her letter in a big fire."
"The Emperor did not want the drink." The reason is not given at A1; consider adding "He did not want to live forever without Kaguya." (as A2 does).

'at once' appears three times ("He loved her at once", "It burned at once", "At once, her heart changed"); it is a fixed phrase some A1 learners will not know. Optional swap: 'quickly' / 'right away'. Not enough unknown items to block comprehension.

Three different robes appear (suitor's robe, Kaguya's robe, the moon robe). The text distinguishes them ('a robe' / 'her robe'), so this is acceptable, but "The moon people put a moon robe on her" would make it clearer.

"But the workers came to the house for their money." The text never says he brought the branch to Kaguya and said it was real, so 'But' has nothing to contrast with. Consider: "He brought it to Kaguya and said it was real. But then the workers came to the house for their money."
"Then I can marry the man with the real thing." 'can' sounds like permission; "Then I will marry the man with the real thing." is more natural.

"He secretly asked workers to make one, but he never paid them. But then they came to the house and asked for their money." Two 'but's in a row and the scene of him presenting the branch is missing. Consider: "...but he never paid them. He brought the branch to Kaguya and said it was real. Then the workers came to the house and asked for their money."
"Even today, smoke still rises from Mount Fuji into the clouds." 'Even today' + 'still' is redundant; drop one.

Second suitor: "Even the old man was convinced" assumes the branch was already presented at the house, which is not narrated. Optionally add "When he brought it to the house, even the old man was convinced...".
"In this world a woman marries" reads slightly stiff; the original sense is closer to "In this world, men and women marry".
"Kaguya began to sit near the edge of the house in the evenings" - 'edge of the house' is vague; "on the veranda" is more natural and closer to the original.

summary: All five levels follow the Taketori Monogatari faithfully (the five impossible tasks, the shadow scene with the Emperor, the two thousand guards, the feather robe, the elixir burned on Mount Fuji) and stay within level grammar and 4+ suitability; the swallow-dung detail is softened appropriately. Quizzes have single correct keyed answers. Remaining points are minor: a missing 'he presented the branch' beat at A2/B1 and a few small wording tweaks.
